economy.summary: His campaign introduction on the Mercer County Democratic Party's candidate page says he will fight for good jobs, fair wages, and economic opportunity for young people in the district.
economy.short: Says he will fight for good jobs and fair wages.

education.summary: Told a local newspaper that improving the public school system is among his campaign priorities; he has served three years on the Sharon City School Board.
education.short: Says improving the public school system is a campaign priority.

healthcare.summary: His campaign introduction on the Mercer County Democratic Party's candidate page says he will fight for affordable healthcare; it does not detail specific proposals.
healthcare.short: Says he will fight for affordable healthcare.

guns.summary: Lists community safety and criminal reform among his campaign priorities in a local newspaper interview; he has not stated positions on firearms specifically.
guns.short: Lists community safety and criminal reform priorities; no firearms specifics.

economy.summary: Told WESA he entered the race to address what he sees as failed policies resulting in seniors and others losing their homes and rising prices of utilities and gas, and describes his campaign focus as affordability, accountability, improvement, and reform.
economy.short: Cites rising utility, gas prices; focuses on affordability, reform.

economy.summary: In a 2022 candidate profile during his previous run for this seat, he ran as anti-inflation and said he supported spurring economic recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic.
economy.short: Ran anti-inflation; supported post-pandemic economic recovery (2022 campaign).

guns.summary: In his 2022 run for this seat, said he supports a strong police force paired with unbiased oversight; he was endorsed by Firearm Owners Against Crime, a gun-owner rights group, and did not detail positions on specific firearms legislation.
guns.short: Supports strong police with unbiased oversight; endorsed by gun-rights group.

economy.summary: Her campaign says she wants to make life more affordable through what it calls common-sense fiscal discipline that focuses on priorities and makes sure the state spends only what it has.
economy.short: Proposes fiscal discipline; state spends only what it has.

taxes.summary: Her campaign describes her as a fiscal conservative who has voted against tax increases 13 years in a row as a North Allegheny School Board member.
taxes.short: Cites 13 years voting against school tax increases.

abortion.summary: Her campaign site criticizes the incumbent for a December 2025 vote on HB 1957, saying he voted to increase abortions in Pennsylvania; the site does not detail her own abortion platform.
abortion.short: Criticizes opponent's abortion-related vote; own platform not detailed.

education.summary: Her campaign calls for accountability, investment, and innovation to make sure kids are prepared to succeed and to help increase parental involvement; she has said she would seek a seat on the House Education Committee, citing 14 years as a school board director.
education.short: Proposes accountability, investment, innovation; more parental involvement in schools.

healthcare.summary: Her campaign says she wants to reduce costs and increase accessibility to quality care.
healthcare.short: Proposes reducing healthcare costs and increasing access to care.

energy.summary: Her campaign site criticizes the incumbent for a May 2025 vote on HB 504, saying he voted to spike utility costs for Pennsylvania families; the site does not detail her own energy platform.
energy.short: Criticizes opponent's utility-cost vote; own energy platform not detailed.

guns.summary: Her campaign says she will support police and emergency responders and bring residents and law enforcement together to meet shared goals; the site does not detail a position on gun policy.
guns.short: Supports police and emergency responders; gun policy not detailed.

economy.summary: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey for this seat, she said she would promote policies that stimulate growth and said Pennsylvania can attract more businesses by streamlining the regulatory process and cutting red tape.
economy.short: Proposes stimulating growth; streamlining regulations to attract businesses.

taxes.summary: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey for this seat, she said taxes can be lowered by reallocating taxpayer dollars to effective programs and reducing unnecessary spending.
taxes.short: Proposes lowering taxes by cutting unnecessary spending, reallocating dollars.

education.summary: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey for this seat, she said she would prioritize strong reading programs as the foundation of learning, advocate for better resources and support for teachers, and emphasize hands-on learning in the curriculum.
education.short: Proposes strong reading programs, teacher support, hands-on learning.

economy.summary: His economic development plank proposes reinvesting in skilled trades and attracting employers who hire locally, saying young people should be able to build a good life without leaving Carbon County. He also proposes restricting institutional-investor ownership of single-family homes and penalties for homes left vacant and land-banked.
economy.short: Proposes reinvesting in trades, local hiring, limiting investor-owned homes.

taxes.summary: Supports full elimination of school property taxes, not rebates or freezes, replaced by a reformed broad-based consumption tax paired with a universal essentials credit, alongside pension reform; says Harrisburg has a spending problem and a discipline problem, not a revenue problem.
taxes.short: Supports eliminating school property taxes; proposes replacement consumption tax.

education.summary: Proposes reinvesting in skilled trades and vocational education so a young person can earn a good living without a four-year degree; this appears within his economic development plank, and his platform does not include a standalone education section.
education.short: Proposes reinvesting in skilled trades and vocational education.

healthcare.summary: Supports expanding nurse practitioner and physician assistant authority in underserved areas, treating telehealth and broadband as essential healthcare infrastructure, and protecting local clinics and hospitals; also proposes tax credits and certification-cost reimbursement to recruit and retain volunteer fire and EMS responders.
healthcare.short: Supports telehealth expansion, rural practitioner authority, protecting local hospitals.

guns.summary: His public safety plank says he will back local police, fire, and EMS with resources and training and defend the constitutional rights of Carbon County residents against efforts in Harrisburg to chip away at them; the platform does not detail specific firearms legislation. His campaign site lists a recommendation from Firearms Owners Against Crime, a gun-owner rights group.
guns.short: Pledges police support, defending constitutional rights; gun-rights group recommends.

economy.summary: In a 2024 candidate questionnaire she strongly agreed that free enterprise and the right to private property are essential to a productive economic system, and said she opposes raising the minimum wage, preferring targeted assistance and workforce development.
economy.short: Backs free enterprise; opposes raising the minimum wage.

abortion.summary: In a 2024 candidate questionnaire she agreed that taxpayer funds should not go to abortion providers and agreed that chemical abortion drugs should meet safety standards.
abortion.short: Opposes taxpayer funding of abortion providers.

education.summary: In a 2024 candidate questionnaire she strongly supported school choice, backing funding that lets dollars follow the child to a public, private, or homeschool option.
education.short: Strongly supports school choice; dollars follow the child.

healthcare.summary: In a 2024 candidate questionnaire she said Medicaid and Medicare should remain available but that no other taxpayer-funded healthcare programs are necessary, and she said she opposes vaccine mandates.
healthcare.short: Keep Medicaid and Medicare only; opposes vaccine mandates.

energy.summary: In a 2024 candidate questionnaire she said stricter environmental regulations cost too many jobs and undermine U.S. energy independence, and identified natural gas as the most reliable energy source.
energy.short: Says regulations cost jobs; names natural gas most reliable.

guns.summary: In a 2024 candidate questionnaire she said she supports reasonable measures such as background checks while upholding Second Amendment rights, and strongly opposed defunding or redirecting funds from police.
guns.short: Supports background checks; opposes defunding police.

economy.summary: His campaign site says he supports fostering a thriving economy with more jobs and opportunities by reducing taxes and regulations to help businesses grow.
economy.short: Supports growing jobs by reducing taxes and regulations.

taxes.summary: He lists fiscal responsibility as a core value, calling for a balanced state budget, cutting wasteful spending, and prioritizing essential services.
taxes.short: Supports balanced budget, cutting wasteful spending, prioritizing essential services.

education.summary: He says he supports empowering parents to make decisions for their children's education and improving education funding and accountability.
education.short: Supports empowering parents; improving education funding and accountability.

healthcare.summary: He says he aims to improve access to affordable care without unnecessary government overreach and backs patient-centered healthcare reforms.
healthcare.short: Supports affordable, patient-centered care without unnecessary government overreach.

energy.summary: He says he supports promoting Pennsylvania's energy independence through responsible resource development while balancing economic growth with environmental stewardship.
energy.short: Supports energy independence through responsible resource development.

guns.summary: His public safety platform says he supports law enforcement officers and implementing policies to reduce crime and protect families; the site does not address firearms specifically.
guns.short: Supports law enforcement; policies to reduce crime.

economy.summary: After securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026, she said her priorities include strengthening local businesses and ensuring that Harrisburg works for the people, not special interests.
economy.short: Says priorities include strengthening local businesses.

taxes.summary: After securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026, she said her priorities include low taxes.
taxes.short: Says her priorities include low taxes.

education.summary: After securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026, she said her priorities include supporting public education; she works as a school nurse.
education.short: Says priorities include supporting public education.

healthcare.summary: A registered nurse, she said after securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026 that her priorities include protecting rural healthcare.
healthcare.short: Says priorities include protecting rural healthcare.
